content.text: {"overall_verdict":"DOES_NOT_MEET_STANDARD","verdict_reason":"The conventional readings of Isaiah 14—“son of dawn,” “north,” “throne,” and “make myself like the Most High”—are admissible and strongly coherent as a unified boast of ascent and usurpation. Several proposed secondary hearings are possible wordplays, but the chapter does not establish their intentional conjunction. In particular, “son and bearer of blackness” is not shown to be a grammatical reading of בן־שחר, “covered lunar seat” blends separate lexical possibilities into one rendering, and the proposed silencing sense of אדמה lacks enough directly applicable grammatical evidence. More decisively, the chapter does not perform Rule 4’s required comparison with the strongest rival joint model: a royal or supernatural usurper ascending to the divine assembly in the north above the stars and clouds. That rival explains the immediate discourse with fewer unsupported steps. The eclipse-and-calendar synthesis therefore remains an interesting hypothesis rather than the demonstrated integrated meaning asserted by the chapter.","rule_audit":[{"rule":"1","result":"PASS","reason":"The chapter expressly retains the received readings and does not argue that Masoretic pointing wins merely by traditional status.
